title: An etale ring map is quasi-finite at every prime (Stacks 00U5)
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then $S$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra and $R\to S$ is quasi-finite [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] at every prime ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $S$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00U5 (lemma-etale-quasi-finite, line 39456) and its proof (fibre rings are etale over the residue fields, hence finite products of finite separable extensions by Lemma 00U3, so quasi-finite by Lemma 00PM lemma-quasi-finite)

proof.text: *$S$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra.* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] (direction 'only if'), since $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is étale [def-weil-etale-morphism], $R\to S$ is an étale ring map in the sense of Algebra, Definition 00U1; in particular $S$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra: $S\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_m)$ as $R$-algebras for some $n,m\ge0$. The images $s_1,\dots,s_n\in S$ of $x_1,\dots,x_n$ then generate $S$ as an $R$-algebra, i.e. $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S$, $x_i\mapsto s_i$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], is surjective; so $R\to S$ is of finite type, which is the standing hypothesis of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. (Stacks: 'By definition $R\to S$ is of finite type.')

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00U5 (lemma-etale-quasi-finite, line 39456), proof, first sentence

proof.text: *The fibre is étale over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.* Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, $\varphi:R\to S$ the given map, with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, an $R$-algebra, and fibre ring $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], with $j:S\to F$, $s\mapsto s\otimes1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] to $R\to A:=S$ (étale by hypothesis) and $R\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$: the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RS)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ induced by $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes1$ is étale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. So $C:=\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RS$, a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra via $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes1$, satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product] with $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. (Stacks: 'the fibre ring $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is étale over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$', i.e. Algebra, Lemma 00U2 (2), base change of an étale ring map.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00U5 (lemma-etale-quasi-finite, line 39456), proof, second sentence; Algebra, Lemma 00U2 (lemma-etale) (2)

proof.text: *The fibre is a finite product of finite separable extensions, hence a finite discrete space.* By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product] (Algebra, Lemma 00U3) applied to $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $C$ of step 2 there are $n\ge0$, fields $L_1,\dots,L_n$ which are finite separable extensions of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and an isomorphism of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebras $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RS\cong L_1\times\cdots\times L_n$. The swap $\tau:S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RS$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes s$, is an isomorphism of rings (its inverse is the swap in the other direction; both are well defined since $(s,\lambda)\mapsto\lambda\otimes s$ is $R$-bilinear) and of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebras, so composing gives a ring isomorphism $\theta:F\to L_1\times\cdots\times L_n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-product-fields] (2) the space $\operatorname{Spec}(L_1\times\cdots\times L_n)$ is discrete. The isomorphism $\theta$ induces the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\theta$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], whose inverse is $\operatorname{Spec}(\theta^{-1})$ by functoriality, so on underlying spaces $\mathfrak Q\mapsto\theta^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$ is a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}(L_1\times\cdots\times L_n)\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is discrete: every one-point subset of $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is open. (Stacks: 'and hence a finite product of fields finite separable over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, in particular finite over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$'.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00U5 (lemma-etale-quasi-finite, line 39456), proof, second sentence; Algebra, Lemma 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] (applied to $\varphi:R\to S$ and $\mathfrak p$) there is a unique prime $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ of $F$ with $j^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q})=\mathfrak q$, the prime of $F$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ in [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. By step 3 the singleton $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}F=\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$, i.e. $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ is an isolated point. Since $R\to S$ is of finite type (step 1), this is exactly the definition [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]: $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$. As $\mathfrak q$ was arbitrary, $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at every prime of $S$. (Stacks concludes with Algebra, Lemma 00PM (lemma-quasi-finite), via finiteness of the fibre over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, i.e. condition (2)/(3) of 00PK; the definition used here is the isolated-point condition (1) of 00PK, which step 3 gives directly from the discreteness of the whole fibre, so the equivalence of 00PK and Lemma 00PM are not needed.)

split_report.summary: Split following Stacks Algebra 00U5 (algebra.tex line 39456; tags 00U5, 00U2, 00U3, 00PM, 00PK verified in tags/tags) in four steps: (1) S finitely presented, hence of finite type, by the ring-level characterization lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine; (2) the fibre kappa(p) (x)_R S is etale over kappa(p) by lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change (00U2 (2)); (3) it is a finite product of finite separable extensions by lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product (00U3), transported to S (x)_R kappa(p) by the swap isomorphism, so Spec F is discrete by lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-product-fields (2); (4) the prime of F over q (lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection) is isolated, which is the definition def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime (isolated point, condition (1) of 00PK); Stacks' final appeal to 00PM (finite fibre => quasi-finite) is replaced by reading the isolated-point condition off directly, as already done in lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points. Statement and stmt_deps kept (correct against 00U5, which states 'an etale ring map is quasi-finite'; the node's 'finitely generated' clause is the 'by definition finite type' sentence of the proof). No new nodes: all cited nodes exist in unit sk-thm-p1. The citer lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-equivalence (step 7) uses only 'R -> B quasi-finite at every prime of B' for an etale B, which the statement gives.
